symptoms: Plants show no signs of disease, robust growth.
pre_management: Ensure soil health through proper nutrient management, Use disease-free and robust planting material.
mid_management: Maintain optimal growing conditions (water, nutrients, and pest control), Regularly monitor for any signs of disease.
future_management: Continue using resistant varieties and improve soil health practices, Implement integrated pest management strategies.
description: Healthy sugarcane is free from any disease or pest. It exhibits optimal growth and high sugar content.

symptoms: Chlorotic or yellowish stripes on the basal portion of the younger foliage, leading to stunted and chlorotic plants.
favourable_conditions: Presence of aphid vectors and infected setts.
disease_cycle: Primary spread through infected canes used as seed.
pre_management: Use disease-free planting material to prevent viral infection, Select resistant varieties if available.
mid_management: Monitor for aphid populations and apply insecticides as needed, Rogue out infected plants immediately to prevent spread.
future_management: Rotate with non-host crops to disrupt the virus cycle, Continue to develop and plant resistant varieties.
precautions: Rogue out the diseased clumps periodically.
description: Mosaic disease is caused by a complex of viruses, typically Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (SCMV). It affects the plant’s leaves, causing a mosaic-like appearance and reduced yield.

symptoms: The first external symptom appears mostly on third or fourth leaf which withers away at the tips along the margins.
cause: Fungal infection causing internal rot of the stem.
favourable_conditions: Monoculturing of sugarcane and waterlogged conditions.
disease_cycle: The fungus is sett-borne and persists in the soil on diseased clumps.
pre_management: Select disease-free planting material and use resistant varieties, Treat setts with fungicides before planting.
mid_management: Monitor fields for symptoms and apply fungicides as needed, Maintain proper irrigation and drainage.
future_management: Practice crop rotation with non-host plants, Regularly scout for disease and remove infected plants.
precautions: Avoid ratooning of the diseased crop.
description: RedRot is a fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum falcatum, affecting the sugarcane stalk. It causes internal decay and discoloration, which leads to weakening of the plant.

symptoms: Minute, elongated, yellow spots appear on both surfaces of young leaves, turning brown on maturity.
cause: Fungal infection caused by rust spores.
disease_cycle: The fungus survives on collateral hosts and infected stubbles.
pre_management: Remove collateral hosts from the area before planting, Use disease-resistant varieties.
mid_management: Monitor for symptoms and apply fungicides as necessary, Ensure proper spacing and air circulation between plants.
future_management: Practice crop rotation to break the disease cycle, Implement integrated pest management strategies.
precautions: Regularly inspect crops for early signs of infection.
description: Rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia melanocephala. It primarily affects the leaves of sugarcane, causing rust-colored pustules.

symptoms: Whitish lines appear on the leaves, run to the full length of leaves and sheaths.
disease_cycle: The bacterium remains viable in the soil and infected canes.
pre_management: Select disease-free planting material, Use healthy setts from disease-resistant varieties.
mid_management: Monitor for symptoms and apply appropriate fungicides, Maintain proper irrigation.
future_management: Practice crop rotation with non-host plants, Regularly scout for disease and remove infected plants.
precautions: Remove infected plants immediately, Practice field sanitation.
description: Yellow leaf scald is a bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas albilineans. It results in yellowing of leaves and can reduce cane yield.
